title: Postgres execute_select_query pastes every clause into raw SQL; SELECT-only guard is a first-word blocklist
reason: select/from/where/join/with/order clauses are tool arguments interpolated straight into SQL; only the first word of select_clause is checked. An injected call can read any table or catalog the connection user can (e.g. from_clause='pg_shadow' or a subquery), call server functions (pg_read_file, dblink, pg_terminate_backend) and use data-modifying CTEs in with_clause; the connection is never committed, which limits but does not remove side effects.
fix: Run the tool with a dedicated read-only DB role (default_transaction_read_only=on, no superuser, only the intended tables); validate table/column names against the inspected schema and build the query with SQLAlchemy Core instead of string clauses; put filter values in bound parameters.

title: ClickHouse execute_select_query/get_table_schema interpolate arguments into SQL without a read-only setting

evidence.quote: schema_name: Annotated[str, "The schema to get the table schema of"],

reason: Clauses and schema/table names from the tool call are pasted into the query; the client is created without readonly settings. A SELECT can use ClickHouse table functions (url(), file(), s3(), remote()) in from_clause, giving SSRF to internal services and local file reads, plus reads of any database the user can see.
fix: Connect with a ClickHouse user that has readonly=1 (or pass settings={'readonly': 1}) and no table-function grants; validate identifiers against system.tables; pass values as server-side parameters.

title: MongoDB read-only blocklist misses $function/$accumulator (server-side JavaScript)
reason: The pipeline comes from the tool call and is checked against a blocklist that only stops $where/$out/$merge and update operators; a stage such as {"$project": {"x": {"$function": {...}}}} with arbitrary JavaScript, or $accumulator, passes and runs inside mongod when server-side JS is enabled (CPU exhaustion / DoS). database_name is also free, so any database the connection can see is readable.
fix: Use an allowlist of pipeline stages and operators, block $function/$accumulator/$unionWith/$lookup to other DBs, connect with a read-only MongoDB role limited to the intended database, and run mongod with javascriptEnabled=false.

title: Worker endpoints fall back to the public secret "dev"
reason: If ARCADE_WORKER_SECRET is not set, the worker's HS256 JWT secret is the well-known string 'dev', so anyone who can reach the worker port can sign a token and list/invoke tools (the base worker refuses to start without a secret, but this path overrides that). The Docker image binds 0.0.0.0. Whether this is exploitable depends on how the port is exposed.
fix: Remove the 'dev' default: refuse to start in HTTP mode unless ARCADE_WORKER_SECRET is set to a random value (>=32 bytes), and bind to 127.0.0.1 unless explicitly configured.

title: Worker secret written to logs on every bad-signature request

evidence.quote: "Invalid signature. Is the Arcade Engine configured with the Worker secret '%s'?",

reason: Any client sending a token with a wrong signature makes the server log the real worker secret in clear text; whoever reads the logs can then forge tokens.
fix: Log only that the signature was invalid (optionally a short hash of the secret), never the secret itself.

title: /mcp HTTP endpoint has no authentication or Origin/Host check
reason: Any client (or a web page via DNS rebinding against 127.0.0.1) can call /mcp without credentials. Impact is limited because tools that need secrets or OAuth are refused on non-stdio transports (server.py:801-803), so only secret-free tools are exposed; check whether your deployment adds tools without declared secrets that touch private data.
fix: Require a bearer token on /mcp and validate the Origin/Host header for localhost deployments.

title: Bright Data scrape returns raw web content to the model
reason: Any page's markdown goes straight into the model context unmarked; text in it can steer later tool calls (e.g. the SQL or GitHub/Stripe wrapper tools if loaded in the same agent). Requests go through Bright Data's API, so this is not SSRF against the local network.
fix: Wrap returned content as untrusted data (clear delimiters / a field like {'untrusted_content': ...}) and keep write-capable tools behind confirmation in agents that also load scraping tools.
